text: Northwind offers three pricing tiers: Starter at $29 per month, Growth at $99 per month, and Enterprise with custom pricing. Each tier includes more seats and higher API quotas.
Every new Northwind account starts with a 14-day free trial of the Growth tier. No credit card is required to begin the free trial, and you can cancel any time before it ends.
The Northwind REST API enforces a rate limit of 600 requests per minute per API key on the Growth tier and 6000 per minute on Enterprise. Exceeding the rate limit returns HTTP 429.
Authentication to the Northwind API uses bearer API keys. Generate an API key in Settings, then send it in the Authorization header as 'Bearer <key>'. Keys can be rotated and revoked.
Enterprise customers can enable single sign-on (SSO) using SAML 2.0. Configure the identity provider metadata URL in Settings under Security, then map SAML attributes to Northwind roles.
Northwind stores customer data in one of three regions chosen at signup: US (us-east-1), EU (eu-west-1), or Asia-Pacific (ap-southeast-1). Data residency is fixed to the selected region.
Northwind takes automated database backups every 6 hours and retains them for 30 days. Enterprise plans can request point-in-time recovery within the retention window.
The Northwind service level agreement (SLA) guarantees 99.9% monthly uptime on the Growth tier and 99.95% on Enterprise. Service credits apply when the uptime SLA is not met.

Support tiers: Starter gets email support with a 48-hour response target, Growth gets 24-hour email support, and Enterprise gets priority support with a 1-hour response target and a dedicated contact.
Northwind can push events to your endpoint via webhooks. Register a webhook URL in Settings, choose the event types, and verify the HMAC signature on each delivery. Failed deliveries are retried.
To reset your password, click 'Forgot password' on the login page and enter your email. Northwind emails a reset link valid for 30 minutes. Set a new password to complete the reset.
Two-factor authentication (2FA) can be enabled per user in Security settings using a TOTP authenticator app. Enterprise admins can require 2FA for all members of the organization.
You can export all of your Northwind data as JSON or CSV from Settings under Data Export. Large exports are generated asynchronously and a download link is emailed when ready.
To delete your account and all associated data, go to Settings, Danger Zone, Delete Account. Deletion is permanent and, per GDPR, all personal data is purged within 30 days.
All Northwind data is encrypted at rest using AES-256. Encryption keys are managed by the cloud provider's key management service and rotated automatically.
All connections to Northwind are encrypted in transit using TLS 1.2 or higher. Older TLS versions are rejected, and HTTP requests are redirected to HTTPS.
Enterprise organizations get audit logs recording sign-ins, permission changes, API key events, and data exports. Audit logs are retained for 1 year and can be streamed to your SIEM.
Northwind uses role-based access control (RBAC) with four roles: Owner, Admin, Member, and Viewer. Permissions are assigned by role, and custom roles are available on Enterprise.
Invite teammates from Settings, Members, Invite. Each invited seat counts toward your plan's seat limit. Starter includes 3 seats, Growth includes 10, and Enterprise is unlimited.
Billing is monthly or annual. Northwind accepts major credit cards and, on Enterprise, invoicing with net-30 terms. Invoices and receipts are available in Settings under Billing.
Northwind offers a prorated refund if you cancel an annual plan within 30 days of purchase. Monthly plans are not refundable but can be canceled to stop future charges.
The Northwind mobile app is available for iOS and Android. It supports viewing dashboards, receiving push notifications, and approving requests, but not full administration.
The maximum file upload size in Northwind is 50 MB per file on Growth and 500 MB on Enterprise. Files larger than the limit are rejected with a clear error message.
Northwind accepts uploads in PDF, PNG, JPEG, CSV, and XLSX formats. Unsupported file formats are rejected at upload time. Uploaded files are virus-scanned before storage.
Northwind integrates with Slack, Microsoft Teams, and Zapier. Connect an integration in Settings to receive alerts and to trigger workflows from Northwind events.
Northwind publishes real-time service health on its public status page at status.northwind.example. Subscribe there to get notified about incidents and scheduled maintenance.
Scheduled maintenance windows occur on the first Sunday of each month between 02:00 and 04:00 UTC. Northwind announces maintenance at least 72 hours in advance on the status page.
The Northwind API is versioned by date in the URL path, for example /v2026-01-01/. Old versions remain available for at least 12 months after a new version is released.
List endpoints in the Northwind API are paginated with a cursor. Pass the 'next_cursor' from a response as the 'cursor' query parameter to fetch the next page; page size defaults to 50.
Northwind API error responses use standard HTTP status codes: 400 for bad requests, 401 for authentication failures, 404 for not found, and 429 when the rate limit is exceeded.
A separate sandbox environment is available at sandbox.northwind.example for testing. Sandbox data is isolated from production and is reset every night at 00:00 UTC.
The Northwind command-line tool, 'nw', lets you script account operations. Install it with 'brew install northwind/tap/nw' and authenticate with 'nw auth login'.
Enterprise customers can serve Northwind on a custom domain with a company-provided TLS certificate. Configure the CNAME and upload the certificate in Settings under Domains.
Email notification preferences are configured per user under Settings, Notifications. You can choose which event types email you, and set a daily digest instead of individual emails.
The Northwind web interface supports light and dark themes. Dark mode can be set per user in Appearance settings or configured to follow your operating system theme automatically.
The Northwind interface is localized into English, Spanish, French, German, and Japanese. Set your preferred language in Settings; dates and numbers follow the chosen locale.
New users are guided through onboarding: create your first project, invite a teammate, and connect an integration. The getting-started checklist appears on the dashboard until completed.
Northwind's deprecation policy gives at least 6 months notice before removing an API field or endpoint. Deprecated fields are marked in the changelog and return a Deprecation header.
Enterprise organizations can restrict access with an IP allowlist. Add trusted CIDR ranges in Security settings; requests from outside the allowlist are blocked at the edge.
The usage analytics dashboard shows API calls, active users, and storage consumed over time. Export the underlying metrics as CSV or query them through the analytics API.
